name: Archaeomancer's Map

abilities.text: When ~ enters, search your library for up to two basic Plains cards, reveal them, put them into your hand, then shuffle.
Whenever a land an opponent controls enters, if that player controls more lands than you, you may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield.

notes: The intervening clause 'if that player controls more lands than you' is written as the core condition opponent-more-lands ('an opponent controls more lands than you'); the two are identical in a two-player game and differ only when a THIRD player has the land advantage instead of the one whose land entered. No core condition names the triggering player's own land count.

issues: Whenever a land an opponent controls enters, if that player controls more lands than you, you may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield. — expected The intervening-if is about THAT player (the controller of the land that just entered): the trigger does nothing unless the specific opponent whose land entered controls more lands than you. — scripted intervening: {kind: 'opponent-more-lands'} — src/engine/characteristics.ts:401 returns true if ANY opponent has more lands than you. In a 4-seat game (the sandbox runs seats4) a land entering under player B lets you drop a land whenever player C is ahead, which the card does not do. No condition kind in src/cards/schema.ts CONDITION_VARIANTS expresses 'that player', so the vocabulary cannot currently say this; the script's notes acknowledge the divergence but the clause is still wrong as written. — CR CR 603.4 (intervening-if), CR 109.5 / 603.10 — 'that player' is the player the trigger event was about

Whenever a land an opponent controls enters, if that player controls more lands than you, ... — expected An intervening-if is checked twice: when the ability would trigger and again as it resolves; if false on resolution the ability does nothing. — scripted src/engine/game.ts:2208 checks ability.intervening only when the trigger is put on the stack and never re-checks on resolution. Engine-side gap, not expressible in the script, but it means the scripted clause is under-enforced. — CR CR 603.4

...you may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield. — expected One 'you may' decision, made by the ability's controller on resolution. — scripted Redundant double optionality: ability-level "optional": true plus the put-from-hand effect's "optional": true. The ability-level flag has no consumer anywhere in src/engine (grep finds no reader of TriggeredAbility.optional), so behaviour is right by accident; the 'you may' is actually carried by put-from-hand's optional → exact:false at src/engine/game.ts:1122. Dead metadata, not a behavioural error.

Whenever a land an opponent controls enters, if that player controls more lands than you, you may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield. — expected The intervening-if names THAT PLAYER (the controller of the land that entered): the trigger only fires when the player whose land entered controls more lands than you. — scripted intervening: { kind: 'opponent-more-lands' } — src/engine/characteristics.ts:401 evaluates `opps.some(pl => lands(pl) > lands(me))`, i.e. ANY opponent. In a 4-player game with opponent A at 3 lands, you at 5, opponent B at 8: A plays a land and the script fires (B is ahead) whereas the real card does not trigger. The script's own `notes` admits this; the condition vocabulary (src/cards/schema.ts:287, types.ts:330) has no that-player variant, so no correct encoding exists today. — CR 603.4 (intervening-if checked on trigger and again on resolution); 109.5 / 'that player' = the player referred to by the trigger event

Whenever a land an opponent controls enters, ... you may put a land card from your hand onto the battlefield. — expected one optionality gate ('you may put') — scripted the ability carries `optional: true` AND the put-from-hand effect carries `optional: true`. Ability-level `optional` is never read by the engine (only src/cards/render.ts:716 consumes it — no reader anywhere in src/engine), so it is dead metadata rather than a bug, but it is a redundant/misleading claim. — CR 603.1

When this artifact enters, search your library for up to two basic Plains cards, reveal them, put them into your hand, then shuffle. — expected up to two, may find fewer; reveal; to hand; shuffle — scripted search count 2, optional true, basic+Plains, to hand, reveal — correct. `exact: !e.optional` (game.ts:1230) lets the player take 0–2, and the shuffle fires unconditionally at game.ts:1239. No issue. — CR 701.19
